title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 64, level structures in char ≠ 2). The previous page attached to a free Z/4-module M of rank 2 the following objects: the octahedron Δ = M*/±1, whose 6 vertices are the points of P^1(Z/4); the set J of its 3 diagonals, J = P^1(F_2); and a 4-element set I, a torsor under V_4 = M_0, with J = P_{2,2}(I), the 3 ways of splitting I into two pairs. Page 39 ('I C') globalises this over a base S and writes a chain of equivalences of data. I read it as follows.

(1) (X, I): X is a genus-0 curve (a P^1-bundle or conic) over S, and I ⊂ X is finite étale of degree 4. For four points on P^1 this is the Kummer/Legendre picture, I = E[2] inside E/±1.

(2) I determines J = P_{2,2}(I), étale of degree 3. J canonically determines:
- V_J, the Klein four-group scheme;
- a genus-0 curve Σ_J with J as its 3 marked points. This is the compactified M_{0,4} for the labelling set I, i.e. the λ-line X(2). Its boundary points are the three pairings, and V_4 acts trivially on cross-ratios, so Σ_J depends only on J.
- Σ_J^* = Σ_J − J.
The cross-ratio of I ⊂ X is then a section t ∈ Γ(Σ_J^*/S). So (X, I) ↔ (I, t).

Since S_4 → S_3 has kernel V_4, I is a V_J-torsor lifting J. Hence (I, t) ↔ (J, t, I a torsor under V_J), and the NB records that t and I are independent data.

(3) Geometric reformulation. Given four points I on X there is a unique Klein subgroup V_I ⊂ PGL(X) acting simply transitively on I. Then:
- X → X/V_I ≅ Σ_J is an abelian V_J-cover, étale over Σ_J^* and with index-2 ramification over J.
- Its fibre over J is the 6 fixed points of the involutions, i.e. the octahedral configuration Δ ('NB X|J ≃ Δ'). This is the cover X(4) → X(2) with its 6 cusps.
- I is recovered as the fibre of X over t.
So the data become (J, t, X a V_J-Galois cover of Σ_J branched over J), with X and t independent.

(4) Such covers are twisted forms of the standard octahedral cover, hence classified by a torsor K under (V_)J. This gives (J, t, K), with K and t independent.

Bottom of the page: when I has a section, I = J ⊔ S, so X has a rational point and there is a canonical iso X ≅ Σ_J. The covering map then becomes a degree-4 endomorphism f: Σ_J → Σ_J, the classical V_4-quotient self-map of P^1 branched at 3 points (the μ ↦ λ, X(4) → X(2) map). The page breaks off here; the next page is an administrative letter.

Overall purpose: a coordinate-free, base-independent description of the λ-line and of level-2/level-4 structures over Z[1/2], as twisted forms over S.
errors: No outright errors are visible. The middle equivalence's wording ('X rev. de Σ_J^*') is ambiguous: as I reconstruct it, X should be the cover of Σ_J (étale over Σ_J^*, ramified over J), not merely of Σ_J^*.
'K torseurs sous J' should presumably be read as a torsor under V_J (or under the Galois structure determined by J); 'torsor under J' taken literally makes no sense.

ideas.what: Cross-ratio of 4 points as a canonical section of Σ_J^*, where Σ_J (the λ-line / M̄_{0,4}) depends only on the set J of pairings, because V_4 acts trivially
ideas.modern_name: M_{0,4} ≅ P^1 − {3 pts} with boundary labelled by pairings; S_4 → S_3 action on the λ-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Klein); moduli version Knudsen, Deligne–Mumford
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4} and P^1 minus 3 points but not this exact formulation

ideas.what: Klein-group cover X → X/V ≅ Σ_J branched at 3 points, with 6-point octahedral fibre over the boundary
ideas.modern_name: X(4) → X(2) (λ-line), octahedral covering, cusps of Γ(4)
ideas.where_published: Octahedral/regular-polyhedra dessins are mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Equivalences of data (X,I) ↔ (I,t) ↔ (J,t,X) ↔ (J,t,K), separating the 'continuous' parameter t from the 'discrete' torsor data
ideas.modern_name: twisted forms / descent description of level structures on the λ-line over Z[1/2]

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, intrinsic (torsor-theoretic) repackaging of classical facts: cross-ratio / λ-line, the Klein four-group, and the octahedral X(4) → X(2) cover. It is nicely canonical, but nothing here would surprise a specialist, and the thread is cut off.
transcription_corrections: Row 3 should read roughly: '(J, t ∈ Γ(Σ_J^*/S), X rev. de Σ_J, étale sur Σ_J^*, ... galoisien sous V_J, ... rev. abélien)'. The '(???) Σ^2) LX' fragment is likely marginal sketch residue.
The NB at top right reads 'X | J ≃ Δ est la configuration [?] octaédrale', i.e. the fibre of X over J is the octahedron.
The bottom line likely reads 'Quand I est muni d'une section, donc tel que I ≃ J ⊔ S, alors on a un iso. can. X ≃ Σ_J, d'où f : Σ_J → Σ_J'.
The right-margin vertical text includes 'P(M_0)' and 'End(M_0)' and appears to be a sketch of the cover/ramification diagram, not running text.
